SUMMONING.
At 10.50 a.m. on the 10-11-33, Mrs. R.D. Keen, residing at the Subankment Building, was driving motor car license No.2068 South to North along the Jessfield Road and when near the Connaught Road she collided with and knocked down a small Chinese boy, age 7, who attempted to run across the Jessfield Road from West to East.
Chapei Police arrived on the scene and requested Mrs. Keen to proceed to the Connaught Road Sub-Station but upon her refusing to comply with their request they took away her driving permit, No. 812 K.
Colonel Tan Bo Shee was later communicated with and the driving permit was handed over to S.I. Stokes.
It was ascertained from Colonel Tan Bo Shee that the child was suffering from "Contusion of Abdomen". Not serious.

At 10 a.m. on the 10-11-33, a party of detectives from the station acting on information received proceeded to the corner of Chungking Road and Avenue Foch and there arrested two Chinese males, one of whom was found to be in possession of a 7.65 calibre pistol and two empty magazines.
Both accused charged with possession of firearms and will appear before Court this A.M. 11-11-33, when a remand will be applied for.

MOTOR CAR HELD
UP ON HUNGJAO
ROAD.
At 6.5 p.m. a telephone message was received from Dr. Bryson, residing at No.567 Hungjao Road, reporting that his wife and a friend had been held up on Hungjao Road by three male Chinese in civilian dress and one in uniform.
Inquiries by S.I. Stokes ascertained that at about 6 p.m. on the 10-11-33 motor car license No.1840 occupied by Mrs. Evan Jones, No.26 Route Ferguson, and Mrs. Bryson, No.567 Hungjao Road, was being driven East along the Hungjao Road by a Chinese chauffeur, and when West of McLeod Road the car was held up by three male Chinese in civilian dress and one in uniform.
Mrs. Bryson was unable to give any description of the man in uniform other than he had a peaked cap similar to that worn by Chapei Police.
The chauffeur of the car stated that the men only asked to be given a lift as far as the Siccawei Police Station but when refused went away without any trouble.
Colonel Tan Bo Shee was informed & promised to have inquiries made into the incident.

1933年11月10日上午10时50分，居住在沙逊大厦（Subankment Building）的 R.D. Keen 夫人驾驶牌照号为2068的汽车，沿极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）由南向北行驶。当行至康纳脱路（Connaught Road）附近时，撞倒了一名试图从西向东横穿极司菲尔路的中国男童，该男童7岁。
闸北警察抵达现场，要求 Keen 夫人前往康纳脱路分巡捕房，但因她拒绝配合，警方扣留了她的驾驶执照，号码为 812 K。
随后与谭伯熙上校（Colonel Tan Bo Shee）取得联系，驾驶执照已移交给巡官 Stokes。
经向谭伯熙上校核实，该儿童患有“腹部挫伤”。伤势不重。

逮捕。
1933年11月10日上午10时，本捕房一组侦探根据所获情报，前往重庆路与福煦路（Avenue Foch）转角处，在那里逮捕了两名中国男子，其中一人被发现持有一支7.65口径手枪及两个空弹夹。
两名被告均被控持有枪械，将于今日上午（1933年11月11日）出庭受审，届时将申请还押候审。

虹桥路
汽车遭劫持。
下午6时05分，接到住在虹桥路567号的 Bryson 医生的电话报告，称其妻子和一位朋友在虹桥路上被三名便衣中国男子和一名身穿制服的男子劫持。
经巡官 Stokes 查询查明，1933年11月10日下午6时许，一辆牌照号为1840的汽车正由一名中国司机驾驶，沿虹桥路向东行驶。车内乘客为住在费格森路（Route Ferguson）26号的 Evan Jones 夫人和住在虹桥路567号的 Bryson 夫人。当车辆行驶至麦高包路（McLeod Road）以西时，被三名便衣中国男子和一名身穿制服的男子拦下。
Bryson 夫人无法描述那名穿制服男子的特征，仅称其戴着一顶类似闸北警察所戴的尖顶帽。
该车司机表示，那些人只要求搭车至徐家汇捕房，但在遭到拒绝后，未生事端便离开了。
已通知谭伯熙上校，他承诺对此事件进行调查。

虹桥。

At about 1.30 p.m. on the 9-11-33, C.P.C.475 on traffic duty at Yu Yuen & Edinburgh Roads was about to arrest two public ricksha coolies for failing to have Settlement licenses when a Bureau of Public Safety Policeman No.5451, who was on duty in the vicinity told him not to interfere with the coolies and ordered him to return the cushions which he had taken from the rickshas. During the controversy, Major Bourne, D.J.Srine, arrived on the scene and instructed the S.P.C. to take the rickshas to the station.
S.P.C.473 alleges that after returning to his post he went to relieve nature in an alleyway off Edinburgh Road and was followed inside by the Chapel Policeman who ordered him out and threatened him with his rifle. This was denied by the S.P.C. who stated that he was called by a shopkeeper to prevent the S.P.C. from urinating at the rear of his shop.
Colonel Tan Bo Hsao was interviewed and stated that Chapel rickshas were issued with a temporary license for the Western Area of Shanghai, and that it was a matter for the Utility Bureau of Greater Shanghai in conjunction with the S.M.C. to determine as where the limits of the license was available (Detailed report forwarded).

At 6.20 p.m. on the 9-11-33, an armed Police search party from the Bureau of Public Safety consisting of three men in uniform and three in plain clothes was seen operating on Jessfield Road near Kinnear Road stopping and searching motor cars and pedestrians.

At 7 p.m. on the 9-11-33, C.P.C.2897 noticed a large crowd of people standing around a public motor car at the corner of Jessfield and Connaught Roads, and upon going to investigate he was abused by a Bureau of Public Safety Policeman who pushed him away. He states that he later saw the car being taken in the direction of the 6th Division Station, B.P.S. by the Chapel Police.
Enquiries made at the above station ascertained that they have no report of the incident. The Johnson Hire Garage was also communicated with but they stated that none of their cars was missing and also that they had no report of the incident.
Enquiries proceeding.
Colonel Tan Bo Hsao will be interviewed this A.M. 10-11-33, when he will be informed of the incident and his cooperation invited to prevent repetition of same in future.

1933年11月9日下午1时30分左右，第475号华捕（C.P.C.475）在虞园路（Yu Yuen Road）与爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）执勤时，正准备逮捕两名因未持有租界执照而违规揽客的公共人力车夫。此时，一名在附近执勤的公安局第5451号警察告诉他不要干涉车夫，并命令他归还从人力车上取下的坐垫。在争执过程中，副督察长 Srine 少校（Major Bourne, D.J.Srine）抵达现场，指示华捕将人力车带回捕房。
第473号华捕（S.P.C.473）指控称，他在返回岗位后，去爱丁堡路旁的一条小巷内方便，一名教堂警察（Chapel Policeman）跟入巷内，命令他出来并用步枪威胁他。但该华捕否认了这一说法，并称是一名店主叫他阻止其在店铺后方小便。
已约谈谭宝昭上校（Colonel Tan Bo Hsao），他表示教堂人力车获发上海西区临时执照，至于执照的有效范围界限，应由大上海公用局与工部局共同确定。（详细报告已呈送）。

向上述分局查询后得知，他们并无此事件的报告。也已联系 Johnson 租车行，但他们表示其车辆无一丢失，且也未收到有关此事件的报告。
调查正在进行中。
将于1933年11月10日上午约谈谭宝昭上校，告知其此事，并请其合作以防止此类事件再次发生。

**〔此处转录不清〕** At 10.45 a.m. on the 22-10-33, two small Chinese boys whilst searching for a marble in a drain in an alleyway situated off the Bubbling Well Road, discovered a .380 revolver. They handed same to a C.P. who brought it to the station. A search of the drain by P.C. Gill resulted in the finding of one round of .380 ammunition.
The revolver appears to have been in the drain for some considerable time and may have been put there by some person to evade arrest.
Same will be forwarded to the Arms Identification Section for examination.
(Station Reference N. 535.)

**〔此处转录不清〕** At 12.30 p.m. on the 22-10-33, a male Chinese named, Yeh Ah Ching, age 30, residing O. R., endeavoured to board motor bus license No. 18004, China General Omnibus Coy. whilst it was in motion, having just started from a stopping place at the junction of Brennan and Jessfield Roads.
He was unable to do so, the door of the bus having been closed by the conductor prior to the bus starting, but continued running alongside the bus until he attracted the attention of bus driver, No. 140, who was off duty and riding in the bus.
He, driver, seeing the pedestrian running after the bus, opened the door to enable him to enter, but the pedestrian failed to keep his balance and fell to the roadway, the rear near-side wheel of the bus passing over his body.
Although S.P.B. ambulance attended, members of the Bureau of Public Safety would not allow the injured man to be removed to hospital and sent him to the 6th Division Station in a public ricksha. He was later removed to the Red Cross Hospital by the S.P.B. Ambulance but was found dead on arrival.
The Inspector in charge of the 6th Division Station was interviewed on two occasions but has refused to allow the body of the deceased to be removed by the Settlement Police for the purpose of an inquest, and placed a guard on duty at the above hospital to see that the body was not removed.
The off duty driver who opened the door of the bus has been detained and will appear before the S.S.D. Court this A.M. No. 18004, when an application will be made for a Writ of Detention, pending further instruction.
D. O. "B" informed.

**〔此处转录不清〕** 1933年10月22日上午10时45分，两名中国男童在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）旁一条小巷的排水沟中寻找弹珠时，发现了一支.380口径左轮手枪。他们将枪交给了一名华捕，后者将其带回捕房。经 Gill 警员对排水沟进行搜索，发现了一发.380口径子弹。
该左轮手枪似乎已在排水沟中放置了相当长的时间，可能是某人为逃避逮捕而藏匿于此。
该枪将送交枪械鉴定科进行检验。
（捕房参考号 N. 535。）

**〔此处转录不清〕** 1933年10月22日中午12时30分，一名名叫叶阿清（Yeh Ah Ching，音译）的30岁中国男子，居住于越界筑路区（O. R.），试图在一辆中国公共汽车公司牌照号为18004的公共汽车刚从白利南路与极司菲尔路交汇处的站点启动时登车。
他未能成功，因为售票员在开车前已关闭车门，但他继续跟随汽车奔跑，直到引起车内一名下班乘车、编号为140的司机的注意。
该司机看到行人追赶汽车，便打开车门让他上车，但该行人未能保持平衡，摔倒在路面上，汽车右后轮从其身上碾过。
尽管工部局警务处救护车到场，但公安局人员不允许将伤者送往医院，而是用公共人力车将其送往公安局第六分局。随后工部局警务处救护车将其转送至红十字会医院，但到达时已确认死亡。
曾两次约谈第六分局主管督察，但他拒绝允许租界警察移走死者遗体以进行验尸，并在上述医院部署警卫，以确保遗体不被移走。
开门的那名下班司机已被拘留，将于今日上午在 S.S.D. 法庭出庭，案件涉及18004号车，届时将申请拘留令，以待进一步指示。

Wednesday 18th Oct. 1933

CHAPEL POLICE
INTERFERENCE ON
MUNICIPAL ROAD

At 7.53 p.m. on the 17-10-33, Mr. Balor, A.C. Traffic, telephoned the station and reported that a short time previously his motor car had been stopped by a party of Chapel Police on Kinnear Road near Jossfield Road, but allowed to proceed without interference when they saw it was a foreigner driving the car.
√ Inspr. Falgetty attended but was unable to locate the police party in the immediate vicinity.
He then proceeded to the 6th Division, B... where the Inspector i/c, after being informed that his officers were exceeding their duty by functioning on Municipal Roads, promised that he would withdraw search parties from Municipal Roads after he had communicated with the Headquarters of the B.F.S.

ARRESTS REPORT.

Reference report Daily State dated 12-10-33, Attempted Highway Robbery. During the period of remand the two accused admitted eleven armed highway robberies in the Bubbling Well and Gordon Road Districts between December 1932 and October 11th, 1933.
In each case, although the majority were not reported to the police, the property stolen has been recovered.
The arrest of the accused was due to the initiative displayed by P.S. Paddoeff and party.

SEARCH PARTIES.

Walking search parties operated in the district from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. the 17-10-33, also from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. the 18-10-33.
During the above hours, 7 motor cars, 10 rickshas and a number of pedestrians were stopped and searched, all correct.

ROADS

No reports.

教堂警察
在工部局道路上
进行干涉

1933年10月17日晚上7点53分，交通股助理督察员Balor先生致电警局报告称，不久前他的汽车在金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）靠近乔斯菲尔德路（Jossfield Road）处被一队教堂警察拦下，但当他们看到驾车者为外国人时，便未加干涉予以放行。
√ Falgetty督察员到场，但无法在附近找到该队警察。
随后他前往第六分区……（原文不清），该分区主管督察员在得知其警员在工部局道路上执勤属于越权行为后，承诺在与法租界警务处（B.F.S.）总部沟通后，将把搜查队从工部局道路上撤出。

逮捕报告。

参照1933年10月12日的每日状态报告，关于企图抢劫案。在两被告还押候审期间，他们承认在1932年12月至1933年10月11日期间，在静安寺和戈登路地区实施了十一宗持械公路抢劫案。
在每起案件中，尽管大多数案件未向警方报案，但被盗财物均已追回。
此次逮捕两被告归功于Paddoeff巡佐及其小队所表现的主动性。

PEACE PRESERVATION CORPS REMOVING ASHES FROM HUNGJAO ROAD.
At 2p.m. on the 16-10-33, Mr. Little, residing at No. 600 Hungjao Road, reported by phone that a number of Chinese Soldiers were removing ashes from the Hungjao Hotel.
Insp. Chamberlain attended and found a large number of members of the Peace Preservation Corps removing ashes, which had been placed on the Hungjao Road by the P.P.C. for road repairs, to the Kau Ka Wei Village for the purpose of making a road from their camp to the Hungjao Road.

保卫团从虹桥路运走灰烬。
1933年10月16日下午2点，居住在虹桥路600号的Little先生通过电话报告称，多名中国士兵正在从虹桥饭店运走灰烬。

ATTEMPTED
MURDER.
TRAFFIC.

At 4.30 p.m. on the 5-10-33, Mr. Ludwig Billing, German,

near house No.200 the front left wheel came off and struck
a Chinese child named Siau hau, age 8, who was standing on
the North side of the road.
The child was removed to the Red Cross Hospital and
found to be suffering from "Contusion of abdomen with
internal bleeding". Not detained.
A Chapei Policeman who arrived on the scene wished to
take Mr. Billing to the Siccawei Sub-Station, R.P.S., but
upon the arrival of S.I. Dalgetty Mr. Billing was allowed
to proceed to Bubbling Well Station.
Particulars of accident given to the Inspector in charge

Bubbling Well
Tuesday 3rd October 1933

INQUEST PROCEEDINGS.
The adjourned inquest proceedings on the body of the late Mr. A.J. Pratt were continued before Mr. J.T. Morris, H.B.M. Coroner, at 10 a.m. on the 2-10-33 when after medical evidence by Dr. Squires had been heard the following open verdict was returned "I find that Arthur Joseph Pratt died on or about the 5th of February 1933 at Shanghai."

PRISONERS CAR SEIZED BY CHAPEL POLICE.
At 8.40 a.m. on the 2-10-33 Mr. L.E. Moeller, German, residing at No.11 Route Delastre, came to the station and reported that his motor car No.6298 was being detained by the Chapel Police.
Inspector Chamberlain proceeded to the 6th Division Station, S.P.S. and there ascertained that at 6 p.m. on the 1-10-33 Mr. Moeller's chauffeur whilst having dinner parked the car in an alleyway in Chinese territory situated off the Bubbling Well Road about 100 yards West of Tifeng Road and upon his return he was arrested by Chapel Police and taken to the 6th Division Station.
Chauffeur fined $20.00 for parking the car in Chinese territory without a Chinese license and allowed to take the car away.

SEARCH PARTIES.
Walking search parties operated in the district from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. the 2-10-33, also from 12 noon the 2-10-33 to 2 a.m. the 3-10-33.
During the above hours, 11 motor cars, 28 rickshas and a number of pedestrians were stopped and searched, all correct.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
4542/1
Date 5 / 10 / 33
Wobbling Well

Monday 2nd October 1933.

ILLEGAL
PUNCTIONING.
At 4 p.m. on the 1-10-33, Mr. W. Richmond, British,
together with Mr. G.R. Moore, British, were riding ponies
on the Rubicon Road near the Lincoln Avenue when Mr. Moore
accidently knocked down a Chinese female, name unknown,
living in a straw hut off Lincoln Avenue.
Mr. Richmond whilst attending to the female, who
sustained a cut lip, was arrested by two Chapel Policemen,
one of whom drew his pistol, and taken to the Poh Sing
Ching Station, B.P.S. where after filling in two forms
admitting committing a breach of the Chinese Traffic Laws
he was allowed to go.
He was later met on the Lincoln Avenue by S.I. Stokes
who proceeded to the above station and asked to be allowed
to see the forms signed by Mr. Richmond. This was not
granted as he was informed that they had already been
forwarded to the Headquarters, B.P.S.

ASSISTANCE TO
FRENCH POLICE.
At 12 noon on the 1-10-33, one named Tsao Kuei Ling,
was arrested as he was about to enter a pawnshop on Avenue
Road to redeem a bicycle from pawn.
The accused at the station admitted having stolen the
bicycle from the French Concession and also confessed to
further larcenies of a similar nature also from the French
Concession. He was closely interrogated regarding similar crimes
in the Settlement but denied having committed any, and on
the instructions of the D.D.C. "A" he was handed over to
the French Police for necessary action.

1933年10月1日下午4点，英国人W. Richmond先生与英国人G.R. Moore先生一起在林肯大道附近的鲁比肯路（Rubicon Road）骑小马时，Moore先生意外撞倒了一名中国女性，姓名不详，居住在林肯大道旁的一间草棚内。

随后，Stokes高级督察员在林肯大道遇见了他，并前往上述捕房，要求查看Richmond先生签署的表格。这一要求未被批准，因为他被告知表格已送至华界警务处总部。

法国警察。
1933年10月1日中午12点，一名叫曹桂龄（Tsao Kuei Ling，音译）的人在进入爱文义路（Avenue Road）的一家当铺赎回典当的自行车时被捕。
被告在警局承认从法租界偷窃了该自行车，并供认在法租界还犯有其他类似性质的盗窃案。就租界内的类似罪行对其进行了严密审讯，但他否认犯有任何此类罪行。根据副警务处处长“A”的指示，他被移交给法国警察以采取必要行动。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / File No. B. REGISTRY / No. D 7543 / Bubbling Well Station / Date 28th July 1933）

REPORT

Subject (in full) Foreigner Stopped by Chinese Officials on Hungjao Road.

Made by ____ and Forwarded by Inspector Glissold.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 11.50 p.m. on the 27-7-33, a telephone message was received from Mr. Meredith, residing at No.158 Route Pichon, French Concession, to the effect that at about 11.15 p.m. the same date he was proceeding along Hungjao Road in his car and that when near the Rubicon Road he was stopped by two Chinese dressed in Kahki uniform and armed with rifles, and two Chinese males in civilian clothes, who told his chauffeur that they wanted a lift along the Hungjao Road as there was some armed robbers in the vicinity. J Glissold

ILLEGAL
AUCTIONING.
At about 10.30 a.m. on the 13-5-33, Motor Bus, license No. 15012, driver No.135, was proceeding East to West on Jessfield Road and when near the intersection of Brenan Road it collided with a cyclist who received slight injuries to the head.
All parties were taken to the 6th Division Station by members of the Bureau of Public Safety where after inquiries had ascertained that the cyclist was at fault, the driver of the bus was released and allowed to take the bus away.
Sgt. Hale attended.

SERIOUS
ACCIDENT.
At about 3.50 p.m. on the 13-5-33, Motor Car, license No.3245, owned by Miss V.C. Buliga, Russian, was being driven West along the Great Western Road by Cpl. Banks, Military Foot Police, Amoy Road Camp, and when a little West of the entrance to the Country Hospital it swerved to the South side of the road and collided with the rear of a stationary Motor Truck, license No.17134, loaded with baskets of sand, driving it forward a distance of 20 feet. The front of the car was completely smashed and the driver of same together with the following passengers were removed to the Country Hospital for treatment: 1/Cpl.s Brockie, Regan & Gretton, all attached to the Military Foot Police. 1/Cpl. Regan only received superficial injuries but the condition of the other three is very grave and they cannot be interviewed.
From statements made by various witnesses it would appear that the car was being driven at a dangerous rate of speed and appeared to be out of control just prior to the collision.
Inquiries proceeding.
(Full report forwarded).

ARREST.
At 10.40 p.m. on the 13-5-33, Det. Laurier, acting upon the authority of an arrest warrant issued by Mr. Haines, British Court Magistrate, proceeded to No.5 Yang Terrace and there took into custody one named, Charles Darwin Williams, aged 51 years, Single, Teacher of languages, on a charge of indecently assaulting young children. He will appear before the B.M.C. Court on the 15-5-33 when a remand will be applied for.
(Detailed report see crime register No.894/33.)

ARRESTS &
SUSPECTED ARSON.
At 12.30 p.m. on the 3-5-33, a fire was discovered at the Novelty Silk Studio, No.762 Bubbling Well Road, managed by one named, M.S. Frankoff, Russian, who at the time of the fire was at Chefoo. During subsequent inquiries a quantity of cotton wool was upon analysis found to be impregnated with ethyl alcohol, and which is believed to have been laid to cause the fire. On the 13-5-33, the following persons who are connected with the store, were taken into custody and will appear before the B.M.C. Court on the 15-5-33 when an application for their detention will be made, pending further inquiries. Names: A.S. Shishkin, I.L. Prunikhoff, D.K. Peshkovsky, S.I. Shikhtmanian.
Detailed report see Crime Register No.894/33.

33年5月13日下午3时50分左右，俄籍女子 V.C. Buliga 小姐拥有的牌照号为3245的汽车，由厦门路军营军事步警队的班克斯（Banks）下士驾驶，沿大西路（Great Western Road）向西行驶。当行驶至乡村医院（Country Hospital）入口稍西处时，车辆向南侧路面偏转，撞上一辆装载沙筐、牌照号为17134的静止卡车尾部，将其向前推动20英尺。该车车头完全损毁，司机及下列乘客被送往乡村医院接受治疗：隶属于军事步警队的布罗基（Brockie）、里根（Regan）和格雷顿（Gretton）三位下士。仅里根下士受 superficial injuries（浅表伤），其余三人伤势危重，无法接受问询。

调查正在进行中。

涉嫌纵火。

At about 8.35 a.m. on the 20-6-33, a chauffeur driven private motor car, license No.2085, occupied by one named, Sung Ma Yuen, a clerk employed at the Bank of China, residing at 493/10 Seymour Road, and a Chinese amah residing at the same address, was about to turn on the Sinza Road outside of the Customs Statistical Dept when four male Chinese, three armed with pistols, approached the car and after intimidating the chauffeur and amah forced them from their seats which were then taken over by two of the kidnappers. The other two sat at the rear guarding the victim while the car was driven west along Sinza Road and South along Kiaochow Road where the kidnappers made good their escape. The car was later found abandoned on Route Ziccawei where it was examined by D.S.I. Read of the Finger Print Bureau but no finger prints could be found.

Patrols were immediately despatched to scour the district and all outlying roads and a message circulated to all stations and French Police, Bureau of Public Safety also notified, all vacant house in the district checked over without result.
Enquiries proceeding.

Foreigner arrested on N. Szechuen Road by Chapei Police.

At 1.58 a.m. 6-10-33 a telephone message was received from Hongkew Station reporting a foreigner having been arrested by Chapei Police.
Inspector Shells well proceeded to the 1st Station 5th Division and there saw a Britisher named K.M. Pate employed at the Shanghai Telephone Company and residing at 1191 Bubbling Well Road from whom the following particulars were obtained. At about 2 a.m. 10-6-33 in company with a friend named R.C. Murray residing at 205 Range Road he was returning to his motor car S.M.C. Lic. No. 3700, which he had left parked on the North Szechuen Road, outside the Isis Theatre. On entering the car he saw a person apparently asleep sitting in the car and at once gave him a push and told him to get out, he then saw that the person was a Chapei policeman, who began swearing in Chinese and then drew his pistol and pointed it at the foreigner. The latter who was also armed and carrying an S.M.P. pistol licence, immediately took out the licence to show the policeman his photograph, at the same time lifting his coat up to show the pistol which he carried in an holster around his waist. The Chapei policeman then tore the half containing the photograph off and also took away the pistol, blowing his whistle at the same time which brought several more Chapei policemen to the scene. The foreigner was then arrested and taken to the 1st Station 5th Division. The Officer in charge of the 1st Station was not present and on arrival of Inspector i/c Dixwell Road, the pistol Colt, .32 S.M.P. No.3931 and 8 rounds of ammunition was handed over and Mr. Pate was allowed to accompany him together with his friend, who in the meantime had reported the arrest at the Hongkew Station. Inspector Shellswell accompanied them to the scene of the occurrence and found the car parked as stated by Mr. Pate. The Chapei Constable's number is 3004.
Mr. Pate is a Sergeant attached to the S.M.P. Specials. Pistol and ammunition handed back to Mr. Pate.
C.J.C.s 3078 and 3324 walking "J beat" saw the foreigner being arrested and immediately informed the Station by phone. Enquiries proceeding.

Correct

Murray）一同返回停在北四川路伊西斯剧院（Isis Theatre）外的汽车（工部局牌照号3700）。上车时，他看到车内似乎坐着一个正在睡觉的人，便推了他一下并让他出去。随后他发现此人是闸北警察，该警察开始用中文咒骂，并拔出手枪指向该外国人。后者同样携带武器并持有工部局警务处手枪执照，立即取出执照向警察展示照片，同时掀起外套展示腰间枪套中的手枪。闸北警察随即撕下带有照片的一半执照，并没收了手枪，同时吹哨召来了几名其他闸北警察。该外国人随后被捕并被带往第五分局第一警局。第一警局主管警官不在场，狄思威路主管督察到达后，移交了一把柯尔特.32口径工部局警务处手枪（编号3931）及8发子弹，佩特先生获准与其朋友一同随督察离开，其朋友在此期间已向虹口警局报告了逮捕情况。谢尔斯韦尔督察陪同他们前往事发地点，发现车辆停放位置与佩特先生所述一致。该闸北警员的编号为3004。
佩特先生是工部局警务处特务队的警长。手枪及弹药已归还佩特先生。
正在“J”区步巡的华捕3078号和3324号目睹了该外国人被捕，并立即通过电话通知警局。调查正在进行中。

At about 10.30 a.m. on the 13-5-33, Motor Bus, license No.
15012, driver No.135, was proceeding East to West on Jesse-
field Road and when near the intersection of Brenan Road
it collided with a cyclist who received slight injuries
to the head.
All parties were taken to the 6th Division Station by
members of the Bureau of Public Safety where after
inquiries had ascertained that the cyclist was at fault,
the driver of the bus was released and allowed to take the
bus away.
S. I. Hale attended.

SERIOUS
ACCIDENT.
At about 3.50 p.m. on the 13-5-33, Motor Car, license
No.3245, owned by Miss V.C. Buliga, Russian, was being
driven West along the Great Western Road by Cpl. Danin,
Military Foot Police, Amoy Road Comp, and when a little
West of the entrance to the Country Hospital it swerved to
the South side of the road and collided with the rear of a
stationary Motor Truck, license No.17134, loaded with
baskets of sand, driving it forward a distance of 20 feet.
The front of the car was completely smashed and the driver
of same together with the following passengers were removed
to the Country Hospital for treatment: 1/Cpl.s Brookie,
Hogan & Gretton, all attached to the Military Foot Police.
1/Cpl. Hogan only received superficial injuries but the
condition of the other three is very grave and they can
not be interviewed.
From statements made by various witnesses it would appear
that the car was being driven at a dangerous rate of speed
and appeared to be out of control just prior to the
collision.
Inquiries proceeding.
(Full report forwarded).

ARREST.
At 10.40 p.m. on the 13-5-33, Det. Laurier, acting upon
the authority of an arrest warrant issued by Mr. Haines,
British Court Magistrate, proceeded to No.5 Yang Terrace
and there took into custody one man, Charles Darwin
Williams, aged 51 years, Single, Teacher of languages, on
a charge of indecently assaulting young children. He will
appear before the B.C.M. Court on the 15-5-33 when a remand
will be applied for.
(Detailed report see crime register No.596/33.)

ARSON &
SUSPECTED ARSON.

Novelty Silk Studio, No.703 Bubbling Well Road, managed by
one man, M.S. Prusloff, Russian, who at the time of the
fire was at Chefoo. During subsequent inquiries a quantity
of cotton wool was upon analysis found to be impregnated
with ethyl alcohol, and which is believed to have been laid
to cause the fire. On the 13-5-33, the following persons
who are connected with the store, were taken into custody
and will appear before the S.A.D. Court on the 15-5-33 when
an application for their detention will be made, pending
further inquiries. Names: A.S. Shidlovsky,
I.L. Frumkinoff, D.K. Puchkovsky, S.E. Shidlovskaya.
Detailed report see Crime Register No.580/33.

Saturday 6th May 1933.

SUICIDE.
At 3.35 p.m. on the 6-5-33, information was received at the station to the effect that a male Chinese had committed suicide by hanging at No.709 Avenue Road.
Inquiries ascertained that at 3 p.m. came unto a tenant of the above house was on the drying stage and upon looking through the window of an attic room saw one named, Yeh Ying Zion, aged 49 years, unemployed, hanging from a rafter in the ceiling. He was immediately cut down upon arrival of the Police sent to the Punkun Hospital but ... found to be dead on arrival. A letter written by the deceased was found in the room stating that he was committing suicide owing to his inability to find employment.
No suspicion of foul play. Body removed to Public Mortuary pending inquest.

ILLEGAL HAWKING.
At 6.15 p.m. on the 6-5-33, a phone message was received from S.P.C.91 reporting trouble with Chinese at Edinburgh & Yu Yuen Roads corner.
Enquiries ascertained that at 5.50 p.m. a Chinese cyclist proceeding North had disobeyed police signals at the above crossing and had returned again at 6.00 p.m. and when passing the S.P.C. had thrown a stone at him. The S.P.C. gave chase but before he could apprehend him the man alighted from his machine and ran to C.P.C.3576, Bureau of Public Safety, who was on duty nearby. The latter insisted that the S.P.C. and cyclist should go to the Bureau of Public Safety Police Station, but upon the arrival of Police from this station the cyclist was arrested and brought to the station where he was charged with assault on Police and disobeying Police Signals.

Friday 21st April 1933.

ARMED ROBBERY.
At 12.45 p.m. on the 20-4-33, one named Tang Sin King,
Shroff, employed by the I.S.C. was standing at the counter
of money exchange shop No.1824 Avenue Road, collecting
license fees, when two men, one armed with a pistol, entered
the shop and after intimidating the inmates stole from the
shroff the sum of J$60.00.
They then left the premises and made good their escape
along the Hai Tan Road.
No alarm raised, no shots fired and no arrests.
Nearest Police to scene of robbery 10 yards away did
not see or hear anything unusual.
Circulated and inquiries proceeding.
Reported at Station at 1 p.m.
(Crime Register No.446).

ARMED ROBBERY.
At 2.50 p.m. on the 20-4-33, six men, three armed with
pistols, entered premises No.32, Lane 403 Yu Yuen Road, by
the unsecured back door, and after intimidating the inmates
stole cash and jewellery to the value of J$40.00.
After remaining on the premises for about 1 hour, the
robbers after covering the heads of the inmates and locking
them in a room, left by point of entry and made good their
escape.
No alarm was raised and no report made to the Station
until 9.10 p.m.
Nearest Police to the scene of robbery 150 yards away did
not see or hear anything unusual.
Circulated and inquiries proceeding.
(Crime Register 452.)

ACCIDENT BY
MOTOR
VEHICLE.
At about 7 p.m. on the 20-4-33, a Japanese Naval Rating
named, Y. Nakatani, was driving Motor Cycle No.1630, North &
South along the Brenan Road, when he collided with and
knocked down a Chinese male who attempted to cross the road
from East to West. Both parties were taken to the 6th Div.
Station by a member of the Public Safety Bureau, where
particulars of the accident was taken and the Marine was
allowed to leave.
No injuries to pedestrian. S.I. Dalgetty attended.

ASSISTANCE TO
FRENCH POLICE.
At 4 p.m. on the 20-4-33, D.J. Taparker, French Police
came to the station for assistance to recover property stolen
in French Concession and pawned at No.215 Putos Road.
Necessary assistance given and property recovered and handed
over on payment of pawn money.

GRAFFITI.
Anti-Japanese slogans were found chalked on a wall on
Great Western Road at 8.30 p.m. on the 21-4-33.
Washed off by Police.

持械抢劫。

随后他们离开现场，沿海坦路（Hai Tan Road，音译）逃逸。
未发出警报，未开枪，无人被捕。
距离抢劫现场最近的警察位于10码外，未看到或听到任何异常情况。
已通缉并正在调查中。
下午1时向巡捕房报告。
（犯罪登记簿第446号）。

持械抢劫。
1933年4月20日下午2时50分，六名男子，其中三人持有手枪，通过未上锁的后门进入愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）403弄32号 premises，在恐吓屋内人员后，抢走现金及珠宝，价值规元40.00元。
劫匪在屋内停留约一小时后，蒙住屋内人员的头并将其锁在一间房内，从来时的入口离开并成功逃逸。
当时未发出警报，直到晚上9时10分才向巡捕房报告。
距离抢劫现场最近的警察位于150码外，未看到或听到任何异常情况。
已通缉并正在调查中。
（犯罪登记簿第452号）。

协助
法国警察。

Tuesday 21st March 1933.

BRITISH COURT PROCEEDINGS.
The adjourned proceedings against David Albert Sullivan, charged with rape from this station on the 2-3-33, was continued before Mr. Haines, Registrar, on the 20-3-33, when he was ordered to be committed for trial on 3 charges, date and time to be notified later.

INQUEST.
The inquest on the body of the late Mr. F.C. Ross was held at the Country Hospital by Mr. Haines, British Court Coroner, at 11.20 a.m. on the 20-3-33. After evidence of identification was given by Mr. F.J. Spgrave, Peach & Coy. the inquest was adjourned until 2.10 p.m. on the 27-3-33.

SLANGS.
Communistic Slogans calling upon the people to join the Red Army were found chalked on the wall on Kinochow Road at 1 a.m. the 21-3-33. Obliterated by Police.

ARMED HIGHWAY ROBBERY.
At 9.50 p.m. on the 20-3-33, a Chinese male named, Ts Foh Hai, residing at No.1060 Yu Yuen Road, was proceeding along the Yu Yuen Road accompanied by his wife when they were held up by two unarmed Chinese males, who after allowing the female to proceed, forced her husband into a lane leading to Chinese territory and there robbed him of clothing and jewellery to the value of $157.00. They then made good their escape into Chinese territory.
An alarm raised, police searched vicinity without success.
Complainant reported to S.P.O.357 at Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads, 600 yards away, who accompanied him to scene of robbery and searched vicinity without success.
Circulars and inquiries proceeding.
Plain clothes police will be posted in this locality with a view to preventing further incidents of this nature.

TRESPASSING.
At 10.15 p.m. on the 20-3-33, five armed Chinese Police, attached to the Public Safety Bureau, were found patrolling the Yu Yuen Road east of Edinburgh Road near the Hotel T'ay Mansion.
When questioned they stated that they had received instructions to patrol that locality.

30th March 1933.

At 9.15 a.m., on the 19-3-33, a report was received at the station to the effect that armed police from the Public Safety Bureau were functioning on the Edinburgh Road.
Insp. Greves attended and found 3 armed policemen functioning on the Edinburgh Road between Yu Yuen and Brenan Roads.
Colonel Tan Bo shee, in charge 6th Division Public Safety Bureau, was interviewed and stated that the shopkeepers on Edinburgh and Brenan Roads had forwarded a petition to the Public Safety Bureau asking for additional police to be posted in these localities owing to number of armed robberies and armed highway robberies that had taken place.
Colonel Tan stated that in view of the petition he had received instructions to open three new sub-stations on the following roads:- Edinburgh Road between Yu Yuen and Great Western Roads, No.885 Brenan Road and Chungshan Road in the vicinity of the Teyedin Cotton Mill.
These stations are in charge of one Sergeant and 10 C.P.Cs and his instructions are to the effect that the police are to patrol the above roads.
D. O. "B" informed.

At 8.45 p.m., on the 19-3-33, three plain clothes policemen attached to the Public Safety Bureau were found functioning on the Kinnear and Joarfield Roads. When questioned they stated they had been posted on the above roads in view of armed robberies that had been committed there recently.
Duties warned.

At 8.30 p.m., on the 19-3-33, Motor car No.412, driven by Hien Kelly Dunst, British Subject, Poulun Hospital, was proceeding West to East on the Great Western Road, 50 yards West of Tunsin Road, when it collided with and knocked down a small Chinese boy who suddenly ran across the road in pursuit of a ball.
Chinese Police from the nearby Sub-Station attended and took all parties to the Station where after particulars of accident had been obtained they were allowed to go.

At 2.55 p.m. on the 6-3-33, Mr. A.J. Silnoff, Russian Bus
Inspector, was examining passengers tickets on the Bremen
Road when a dispute arose between him and 2 members of the
China Peace Preservation Corps as to the validity of their
tickets.
A scuffle ensued and all parties were taken to the 5th
Division Station where later on the representations of J.I.
Hale and Mr. Suberman, Bus Company, the Bus Inspector was
released.
Colonel Tan De Sheo, Chief of the 6th District Station
had no jurisdiction over the Peace Preservation Corps but would
forward a report of the occurrence to their Headquarters.

DEAD BODY.
At 4.15 a.m. on the 6-3-33, the dead body of a male Chinese
of the beggar class was found in an alleyway off Yu Yuen Road
near Edinburgh Road.
As foul play suspected, the Finger Print Bureau and Dr. Lieu,
Police Hospital, were informed, but as a result of enquiries
made by detectives and the medical examination, it was
ascertained that the deceased died from natural causes.
Officials from the Bureau of Public Safety and a judge from
the Nantao Court attended the scene, and after viewing the body
ordered it to be removed as it was lying in Chinese territory.
D. O. "B" informed. (Detailed report forwarded).

SEARCH PARTIES.

Bubbling Well

Wednesday 11th January 1933.

At 9.30 a.m. on the 10th, Mr. H. Middleton (British) residing at No.397 Great Western Road, reported that at about 9.30 p.m. on the 9th, he was walking along Great Western Road accompanied by his wife and when about 200 yards from the Railway Crossing; they were held up by 4 or 5 members of the Peace Preservation Corps or Chapel Volunteers. One of the men held a pistol to Mr. Middleton's stomach whilst another pushed a rifle against his wife, in consequence of which she received a severe shock. After speaking in Chinese which Mr. Middleton did not understand the men indicated that they could proceed no further. Mr. Middleton and his wife then returned home. Inspector Groves and Inspector Chamberlain visited the Officer in charge of the Peace Preservation Corps off Great Western Road, who stated he had received no report from any of his men regarding this incident. He stated that his men do not function on the roads.

At 11.40 a.m. on the 10th, F.J. Page reported that a serious accident had occurred at Breman Place and the Chapel Police had taken the chauffeur and M/car to the 6th Division Station.
From enquiries made it was ascertained that M/car No.10087 owned by Lee Yung Sai, No.136 Avenue Haig, driven by Yih Tsang Hai e/e employer, was proceeding North on Breman Road when he swerved to avoid colliding with a cyclist and struck a pedestrian named Woo Leung residing at No.1400 Ferry Road. The injured person was removed to the Red Cross Hospital in the Fire Brigade Ambulance and detained. Medical Certificate: Compound Fracture, tibia & fibia and abrasion of right eye brow.
J.I. Hale proceeded to the 6th Division Station where the chauffeur was detained and requested the officer in charge to hand him over to the S.M. Police as the accident occurred on the Municipal Road. This request was refused.

At 6.5 p.m. on the 10th, C.P.0.645 reported that a male Chinese was found unconscious in Trailer Tramcar No.186 which was proceeding East along Avenue Road. He was immediately removed to the Peking Hospital and certified to be dead on arrival. From enquiries made it was ascertained that deceased named Wong Ah Chuen age 62, was employed as a Tinsmith at No.88 Tseping Road and was returning home from work. In suspicions of foulplay. Body removed to the Public Mortuary pending Inquest.

At 3.30 a.m. on the 11th, C.P.0.1434 brought to Station a male Chinese, Tsang Ah Yee, whom he arrested in Bubbling Well Road near Yueng Haig in possession of a human head, apparently of a male Chinese aged about 30 years.

静安寺

1933年1月11日，星期三。

10日上午9时30分，住大西路397号的英国人H. Middleton先生报告称，9日晚约9时30分，他与其妻沿大西路行走，行至距铁路道口约200码处时，被4或5名保安队或教堂志愿队成员拦截。其中一人用手枪顶住Middleton先生的腹部，另一人将步枪抵住其妻子，致使其受到严重惊吓。这些人用中文交谈，Middleton先生听不懂，随后示意他们不得继续前行。Middleton先生及其妻子随即返回家中。Groves巡官和Chamberlain巡官拜访了驻大西路附近的保安队负责人，该负责人表示未收到其下属关于此事件的任何报告。并称其人员不在道路上执行任务。

10日上午11时40分，F.J. Page报告称，在Breman Place发生了一起严重事故，教堂警察已将司机及机动车带至第六分区捕房。
经查询获悉，海格路136号Lee Yung Sai所有、由其雇员Yih Tsang Hai驾驶的10087号机动车，沿Breman Road向北行驶时，为避让一名骑自行车的人而转向，撞倒了一名住在渡船路1400号、名为Woo Leung的行人。伤者由救火会救护车送往红十字会医院并留院观察。医生证明：胫骨和腓骨复合性骨折，右眉擦伤。
J.I. Hale前往第六分区捕房，司机被拘押于此，他要求负责警官将其移交给工部局警务处，因为事故发生在工部局道路上。该要求被拒绝。

10日下午6时05分，C.P.0.645报告称，在沿爱文义路向东行驶的186号拖挂电车内发现一名昏迷的中国男子。该男子立即被送往同仁医院，抵达时被证实已死亡。经查询获悉，死者名为Wong Ah Chuen，62岁，在乍浦路88号担任白铁匠，当时正下班回家。疑为他杀。尸体已移送公共停尸房，以待验尸。

11日凌晨3时30分，C.P.0.1434将一名中国男子Tsang Ah Yee带至捕房，该男子是在静安寺路近杨海格（音译）处被捕的，当时他持有一颗人头，看似属于一名约30岁的中国男子。
后续调查使侦探们相信，这颗人头取自Great **〔此处转录不清〕** 附近的一具尸体。
进一步调查中。
